causes.what: The reference pages draw every stroke in the file with butt caps and miter joins. The SVG's root asks for round caps and joins on all of them, and femtovg (through usvg) draws them round, as the file says. So at every stroke end and corner the browsers put down less ink than femtovg. At hd that is 785 of the 815 red px: brow hairs, hair strands, eyelid/crease/lash strokes and mouth strokes. femtovg is the one that is right. causes.elements:
The root element, gpt-6-astra.svg line 1: <svg ... stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round">. Every stroke without its own cap inherits it. By hd px: brow hairs, lines 337-348 (157 px); hair strands, lines 581-811 (427); eyelids, creases and lashes, lines 373-411 (84); mouth and teeth strokes, lines 474-531 (59); face wrinkles (58). At z2: 12 brow, 17 hair, 5 eye, 4 mouth.

Harness: da/harness/make_ref.py, `keep = " ".join(a for a in re.findall(r'\b(?:fill|stroke|fill-rule|opacity|style)="[^"]*"', attrs))`. It carries only those five names onto the nested <svg>. refs.py, refs_webkit.py and refs_ideal.py all build their pages with make_ref.py, so Chromium, Firefox, WebKit and the 8x area reference all lose the caps.
causes.mechanism:
make_ref.py frames the file in a nested <svg> and copies the root's presentation attributes onto it. It copies only fill, stroke, fill-rule, opacity and style, so stroke-linecap and stroke-linejoin are lost. In all four references every stroke then gets the initial butt cap and miter join. usvg resolves the root's presentation attributes and the harness strokes with round caps and joins.

The difference at each end is a half-disc of radius half the stroke width (1.2 px for the 2.2-unit brow hairs at hd). The brow hairs show it best: femtovg draws the hair colour (217,199,162) at the end pixels, where the references show only the brow fill.

The same regex also reads fill-opacity="..." as opacity="...", because \b matches after the hyphen. Of the 1,269 SVGs under da/corpus, gpt-6-astra.svg is the only one with a root stroke-linecap or stroke-linejoin. Two firefox glyphs (glyph-pin-16, glyph-modal-delete-20) have a root fill-opacity. They are emitted as opacity="context-fill-opacity", an invalid value that is ignored either way.

causes.mechanism:
PathCache::expand_stroke (src/path/cache.rs:1035 at 06243b80) sets ncap = curve_divisions(half_width, PI, tess_tol), with TESS_TOL 0.125.
- Half widths up to 0.81 px get 3 rim points. That covers every stroke up to 1.6 px wide, including all strokes under 1 px, which are drawn 1 px wide with scaled alpha.
- Up to 3.0 px wide they get 4 points, up to 4.9 px 5.

round_cap_start and round_cap_end place the rim points at half_width + fringe/2 and fan them to the centre at u=0.5. The cap is therefore a triangle or a half-square. Its chords cut the AA ramp at the diagonals, so coverage drops to zero well inside the true arc there. round_join clamps its divisions to the same ncap.

The lower-tooth corner (391,730) stays red with miter joins as well, so it is an under-ink on the inner side of an acute join, not tessellation alone. It is isolated (it goes away with the teeth strokes removed), but its mechanism is not proven.

per_cause.reason:
The core claim holds and is now proven by emulation. The source matches the report:
- ncap = curve_divisions(line_width*0.5, PI, 0.125) at cache.rs:1035.
- The rim radius is half width + fringe/2, and the fan's centre vertex has u = 0.5.
- round_join clamps to ncap (.min(ncap)).
- The width thresholds (3 points up to a 1.6 px stroke, 4 up to 3.0 px, 5 up to 4.9 px) check out.

In the corpus, flipping both sides to butt/miter (svg/v01_butt.svg) clears exactly the 9 hd cap/join px and the 1 z2 px. All of them are femtovg under-ink.

scripts/emu.py rebuilds femtovg's triangle strip (round_cap_start/end) with linear u and strokeMask at pixel centres. It matches the harness frame within 1 level at every cap pixel of svg/r1_round.svg (widths 1.2-8 px, z1/z2). With 64 rim points the same emulation leaves 0 px more than 20 off the area ref (1 px at 2.0 px), against 1-8 px per cap on master.

Control: svg/r1_fillcap.svg draws the same caps as a filled rect+discs. At 3-6 px width it lands at 1.003-1.024 of area-ref ink, while the stroked caps land at 0.86-0.95.

Three parts of the report need correcting:
- Scope: the error does not stop at about 3 px. At z2, 6 and 8 px strokes still have 3-8 px more than 20 off the area ref per cap (ink 0.95-0.97).
- Shape: the 4-point case is a half-hexagon, not a half-square (the triangle and the 'half-square' are the same shape).
- The tooth corner now has a mechanism; see below.
per_cause.corrected_mechanism:
Same core: a fan of ncap rim points, so the u=0 contour runs along the chords and the AA ramp is cut short on the diagonals. Two things make the chords sag 0.17-0.37 px, against tess_tol 0.125:
(1) ncap is chosen from the half width r, but the rim sits at r + fringe/2.
(2) curve_divisions returns a number of chords, while round_cap_*/round_join use it as a number of points, which gives ncap-1 chords (an off-by-one that nanovg shares).
Emulating ncap = curve_divisions(r+fringe/2)+1 clears everything up to 4 px wide; 6 px still needs more points.

The lower-tooth px (392,731) is a different bug, now proven: under-ink at the inner corner of a join, and not specific to acute angles. For a non-bevel join, expand_stroke emits the pair p1 +/- dmpos*w. The two segment quads share that edge, so u is interpolated linearly from the outer to the inner miter vertex. A pixel at the inner corner, where both inner edges meet, then gets the single-edge ramp value. The true coverage there is 1 minus the share of the wedge between the two inner edges.
Reduction: svg/r2_innerjoin.svg, an open 1.27 px polyline with a miter join at 45/61/90 degrees and 12 subpixel offsets each. scripts/emu_join.py matches femtovg within 1 level at all 36 inner-corner px. femtovg sits 20-80 levels under the area ref, e.g. 174 vs 240, 89 vs 163, 88 vs 129 at 90 degrees. That gives 43 px off all three and 23 within 1 px of an inner corner, at 90 degrees too.
In the corpus pixel, femtovg 191 vs area 165 (all browsers 164-165) sits right at the inner miter point of the 61-degree closing vertex of the 1.2-unit tooth stroke. It belongs in the same issue as a second item, now proven, not 'unproven'.

per_cause.what: 6. Round caps of thin hair strokes (lines 610–645): 10 red at hd.
per_cause.reason:
The symptom and the mechanism hold:
- Butt caps (v06) remove exactly those 10 pixels at hd, and z2 does not change.
- At those pixels femtovg is 20–60 off the area reference; the best browser is 0–4 off.

**The code check is wrong.** The harness calls set_size(..., 1.0), so tess_tol = TESS_TOL / dpi = 0.125, not 0.25. With the right value:

| Half-width (px) | ncap |
|---|---|
| 0.63, 0.79 (the 1.2–1.5 unit strokes) | 3 |
| 1.05, 1.32 (lines 617 and 616) | 4 |
| 1.58 | 5 |

The count never drops to 2. That would need a half-width under 0.30 px, and expand_stroke never sees one: strokes thinner than the fringe are widened to a half-width of 0.5.

**Measurement.** capmodel.py models femtovg's cap fan: rim at hw+0.5, u=0.5 at the centre, the shader's stroke_mult. Over 35 straight strokes of 1.2–3 units at seven angles (r40), it matches femtovg within 0.004 everywhere.
- femtovg's end ink is 0.97x the area on average (range 0.93–1.01). The end windows have 101 px more than 20 off the area.
- Taking ncap from the outer radius (hw+0.5), as the todo suggests, gives 0.994x and 39 px in the model.
- Round joins use the same ncap. In r27, the outer corners at 90° come out 36–82 levels too light.
per_cause.corrected_mechanism:
Each round cap is a fan of ncap−1 triangles, with ncap = curve_divisions(hw, π, 0.125). The rim sits at hw + fringe/2 and the ramp falls to 0 on the chords, so the cap is drawn as the inscribed (ncap−1)-gon of radius hw.
- For the 1.2–1.5 unit strokes (ncap 3) that is a triangle.
- For lines 616 and 617 (ncap 4) it is three chords.

Per cap, the ink falls short by (π/2 − (n/2)·sin(π/n))·hw² px², where n = ncap − 1.

The fix as proposed: compute ncap from hw + 0.5, or set a minimum. Apply it to round joins too, and check the frame-time cost on the card pages.

causes.what: Single wrong pixels at sharp corners of fills that are not slivers. A convex corner gets about 0.5 coverage at the pixel on its vertex where the pixel's area share is the wedge's (0.25 at 90 degrees, less when sharper); a reflex corner (notch) gets the reverse. This shows up on pareto's zigzag hair outline (straight-sided spikes of 41-101 degrees and notches of 48-108 degrees) and on tooth, nostril and eyebrow corners elsewhere.
causes.mechanism:
femtovg's fill antialiasing is a fringe: a linear ramp per edge, 0.5 on the edge line, with neighbouring edges' ramps joined at a miter. That is right along an edge but not within about half a pixel of a vertex. There a pixel's area share is the wedge's fraction, while the ramp still reads about 0.5.
- Convex corners over-ink: 0.5 against 0.25 at 90 degrees, and against about 0.11 at 41 degrees.
- Reflex corners under-ink: 0.5 against 0.75.
- Below about 45 degrees the error spreads over the tip, and the corner becomes a mild case of (a).
This happens on convex paths (inset fan plus half fringe), on concave stencil paths, and on straight edges, not only on flattened curves. Exact-area coverage removes it. It is the same corner error #380 removed for clip shapes by taking the product at a square corner.

causes.elements: claude-sonnet-5-5 L268-270: `<g mask=url(#stubMask)><rect width=1024 height=1024 filter=url(#stubble) opacity=0.75/>`. Filter stubble (L96-99): feTurbulence fractalNoise baseFrequency 0.85, numOctaves 2, seed 7, then feColorMatrix with alpha = 12R - 6.1.
causes.mechanism:
At 0.85 cycles per user unit the noise runs at 2.2 cycles per device pixel at z2 and 0.8 at hd. That is above what one sample per pixel can represent, so each engine's choice of sample points and resolution gives different values. The 12x alpha gain turns small differences into 0/1 flips of the stubble dots.
- femtovg and Firefox produce the same pattern.
- Chromium's differs.
- WebKit's matches Chromium at hd but not at z2, which suggests it rasterises the filter at a different resolution at that scale.
- The 8x area reference is Chromium's noise averaged down, so it is not ground truth for this region.
causes.known_issue: None. It is the browsers' own disagreement (c), on an feTurbulence input.

per_cause.corrected_mechanism:
The mechanism is right; this is the exact path in src/path/cache.rs expand_fill. A concave fill's stencil fan is inset by woff = 0.5 px along each point's miter vector. Its fringe is a 2 px strip running from 1.5 px inside to 0.5 px outside (u 0 -> 1, alpha peaking 0.5 px inside), drawn only where the stencil is 0.

- So the stencil leaves the tip uncovered. Both sides' full fringe strips then paint there, overlap each other and spill past the opposite edge.

per_cause.corrected_mechanism:
The mechanism is right, but 'about 0.5 at the vertex' only holds for a vertex on the pixel centre. In general the vertex pixel gets the minimum of the per-edge ramps (axis-aligned: min(a,b) against a*b), so the error is min(a,b)*(1-max(a,b)), which peaks at 0.25.

It is not specific to fills. The same mitered linear ramp makes a stroke outline's corners wrong too. In svg/v_miter.svg (30-60 degree joins, 1.5-10 px wide), the miter tip pixel is +0.25 to +0.30 and the inner crotch -0.25 to -0.31; 42 px are off all three at hd, with total ink conserved.

Butt-cap corners are exact, because the stroke shader multiplies the across-ramp by the along-ramp. The issue title should say 'polygon outline corners (fills and stroke joins)'.

per_cause.what: Round caps on thin strokes come out short (24 px, 10 %)
per_cause.reason:
The symptom and the root cause (a coarse cap fan) are right, but the stated thresholds are wrong. Master's TESS_TOL is 0.125 (src/lib.rs:391, tess_tol = TESS_TOL/dpi); the investigator's numbers fit 0.25.

Sweep (svg/v_caps.svg, scripts/caps.py, caps2.py): horizontal and 35-degree lines at 13 device widths and 4 sub-pixel phases, against an analytic stadium.
- Round-cap ink is 0.86-0.95x at widths up to 1.6 px, then steps to 0.96-0.97x at 1.7 px. It drops again 3.0 -> 3.1 px: 0.917 -> 0.971.
- Those steps are exactly where curve_divisions(r, PI, 0.125) goes from 3 to 4 to 5.
- Butt caps are exact (0 px).
- Femtovg is off all three on 57, 64 and 122 cap pixels in the thin, mid and wide sets. It still has 43 px over 20/255 at 6 px.

In situ:
- Rewriting 74 opus strokes as butt caps plus discs (svg/o_v_capdiscs.svg) clears 2/2 cap pixels at z2 and 15/15 at hd, measured against the variant's own four refs.
- A targeted rewrite clears sol L361/L362 at hd (2/2).
- One element is misattributed: sol z2 (168,212) is the cap of L633 (stroke-width 4, 1.56 px), not L651. Rewriting L633 alone brings that pixel to exactly the area value (219,161,123 -> 196,140,106).
per_cause.corrected_mechanism:
expand_stroke computes ncap from r = half the device width with tess_tol 0.125:
- ncap is 3 (a two-chord diamond) only for widths up to about 1.62 px (r <= 0.81).
- It is 4 up to about 3.03 px and 5 up to about 4.9 px.
- It is never 2: strokes under the fringe are widened to 1 px first (lib.rs, the line_width < fringe_width branch), so r >= 0.5 gives 3.

The defect that persists at every width is the off-by-one. curve_divisions returns a segment count, but round_cap_start/end emit ncap points, which is ncap-1 chords, so the chord sagitta (r*(1-cos(pi/(2(ncap-1)))) at the 50 % contour) stays above tess_tol.

The rim at r + fringe/2 is just the alpha-0 line, not a separate error.

round_join has the same off-by-one. It uses n = ceil(turn/pi*ncap) points, clamped to [2, ncap], so on strokes up to 1.62 px every round join with a turn of 120 degrees or less is a bevel. Example: sonnet z2 (117,13) is 0.13 against an analytic 0.58.

Fix: emit ncap+1 points per half circle, in round_cap_start, round_cap_end and round_join.
